answer: A reputation grove works like this: every agent earns trust only through verified work over time, and trust decays if it goes idle, so a fresh fake identity starts at zero and must pay real compute and time before it can trade. Attackers face a spiral of cost, each new identity repeating that slow climb, while a shared stake that can be slashed acts like a vine binding reputation to a deposit, making mass fakery expensive and easy to prune.
